title: Anticipatory quota enforcement for multiplexed streaming with speculative outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe rare but high-severity cases where multiplexed real-time streams (multiple logical conversations on a single connection) generate speculative tokens that are later rolled back or superceded due to midstream model switch, cancellation, or deterministic reranking. Current billing behavior either (a) conservatively charges on every speculative frame leading to unexpected customer debits, or (b) defers charging until finalization which can allow negative available quota during sustained high-throughput streams. Both outcomes create customer dissatisfaction and operational headaches for SRE/billing reconciliation.

Goal: Design and implement an anticipatory quota enforcement model that: (1) prevents customers from being overdrawn but also avoids spurious immediate charges for tokens that are never finalized; (2) preserves low-latency streaming SLOs; (3) integrates with existing billing ledger and reconciliation pipelines; (4) supports multiplexed sessions and reconnects with idempotency and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc merged describing provisional debit model, lease semantics, commit/rollback protocol, and API for clients to opt-in/out
Prototype integrated into stream ingress that attaches provisional_debit records to session IDs and idempotency keys
E2E simulator demonstrates no customer ends up with negative available quota under 10k simultaneous multiplexed streams in our stage cluster
Reconciliation job has metric that counts provisional_debit -> final_commit mismatches and it is below 0.01% after 24h of synthetic load
Observability: dashboard shows provisional vs committed token tallies, and alerts on >0.1% unexplained provisional aging beyond 1 hour
Billing audits produce deterministic per-session traces (linkable to sids) for every charged token
Automated unit + integration tests covering disconnects, reconnects, midstream model switch, speculative aborts, and duplicate frames
technical_notes:
High-level approach: issue a short-lived provisional token lease when the runtime emits speculative output frames. Provisional debit objects live in the metering service with state {provisional, committed, rolled_back} and expiry TTL (default 10 minutes). On finalization (terminal token or explicit commit event) we atomically commit provisional debits to the ledger; on abort or TTL expiry a background reaper rolls back and produces a reconciliation record. Key invariants: (A) every committed token must be backed by a provisional record or an explicit one-shot commit; (B) ledger commits must be idempotent keyed by (session_id, stream_seq, provisional_id).

Lease sizing: default provisional charge equals lit-inference token estimate for the frame; to avoid customer surprise we apply a conservative factor for new accounts. For enterprise tiers we expose a config to allow optimistic provisional-only charging with higher TTL.

Performance: path keeps latency-critical hot path minimal: issue provisional_debit as a best-effort async write to a fast, durable store (rocksdb/redis-streams + write-ahead to Kafka). The commit path is synchronous only when finalizing terminal frames or when a customer's available quota would otherwise be exceeded.

Reconciliation: build a daily aggregation job to detect long-lived provisional_debits and reconcile with ledger with a human-auditable CSV for billing support. We also emit anomaly events to the ops incident pipeline when rollback rate spikes.

Trade-offs considered: conservative immediate charging avoids post-hoc refunds but penalizes customer experience; purely optimistic booking simplifies UX but increases risk of quota exhaustion and failed requests. The chosen hybrid balances UX with safety, while adding complexity and operational surface area.
